text:
mike: heads up — seeing a pattern of intermittent CUDA OOMs on a subset of inference nodes in us-west-2, started ~10m ago. containers are restarting; svc error rate up 3-4x for a handful of customers. suspect paged-attention allocator / kvcache fragmentation (slow memory creep).

incident-bot: Incident created — INC-2026-042: paged-allocator fragmentation causing node-level CUDA OOMs (severity: P2). Assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

sasha: confirming — logs show repeated: "CUDA out of memory while allocating X KB" coming from attention_pager.cc:allocPage. Also seeing lots of small free/alloc churn for kvcache pages.

anoop: do we have the slab/bitmap metrics for affected GPUs? can we pin which pool this is?

mike: affected pool: gpu-pool-inference-6 (nv4a series). slab bitmap shows high fragmentation: free segments present but unable to satisfy contiguous page requests after paging ramp.

jing: looks like attention paging is trying to allocate ~48MB pages but fragmented into many small holes. eviction metrics show kvcache_evictions=0 despite high page churn. curious why eviction not kicking.

leo: rolling restart wouldn't fix fragmentation if allocator state persists (it will on node restart yes, but container restart may not). stateful allocator resides in the driver process on the node.

mike: immediate mitigation options I can do now: 1) enable emergency kv-evict-mode=aggressive (feature flag), 2) temporarily disable attention paging for this pool (fallback to CPU attention — increases latency but avoids OOM), 3) drain the worst nodes and reprovision. thoughts?

sasha: agree order: try kv-evict-mode first since lowest customer impact. need a quick way to flip per-pool config.

mike: patch ready, will flip for gpu-pool-inference-6: 
```bash
# emergency toggle
curl -X POST "https://control-plane/api/pools/gpu-pool-inference-6/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_API" \
  -d '{"kvcache_eviction_policy":"aggressive"}'
```

deploy-bot: patch applied to gpu-pool-inference-6 by mike at 1736009380.

jing: after flip, eviction rate jumped ~20x on those nodes. memory reclaim increased. are OOMs still happening?

mike: 6m after flip: OOMs dropped substantially but not zero — 2 nodes still saw single OOM and auto-restarted. error rate trending down.

natalie-oncall: customer impact: a small subset of customers on dedicated capacity in us-west-2 may have seen request failures and degraded latency for ~20 minutes. CS alerted for any escalations. tagging customer-signal channel.

leo: for the remaining nodes we should also schedule a rolling node reboot during a low-traffic window to defragment allocator state. I'll open a ticket to repro and validate persistent leak vs fragmentation.

anoop: investigation notes: potential root causes — 1) allocator bitmap not consolidating freed pages due to rare race in paged-allocator free path, 2) certain requests allocate unusual page sizes that fragment common slab bins, 3) eviction threshold too conservative for this workload pattern.

jing: can we instrument a per-request page-size histogram and include kv-key prefix to see if a particular model causes the fragmentation?

mike: adding a quick trace patch to collect page-size histograms for the pool (low-overhead sampling) and will ship to us-west-2 canary.

deploy-bot: canary deployed to 2 nodes in gpu-pool-inference-6 at 1736009920.

sasha: oncall action items: 
- keep kv-evict-mode=aggressive for the pool until kap 24h stability
- schedule rolling node reboots for affected nodes tonight 02:00 UTC
- run allocator free-path repro harness against canary image
- collect per-request page-size histograms + top models

mike: also proposing a short-term config to limit attention-page allocation size to 16MB to reduce contiguous allocation pressure (tunable). will test on canary.

leo: customer comms: send a short summary to affected customers outlining root cause suspicion (fragmentation leading to OOMs), what we did (eviction mode + canary + reboots scheduled), and mitigation plan. keep tone: apologetic + technical.

natalie-oncall: i'm handing off to night oncall (sasha) — will update incident doc and notify CS. @sasha you're primary for next 8h.

sasha: taking it. watching metrics/dashboards. if we see OOMs again, escalate to full pool-disable fallback (disable paging globally for pool) and route traffic to alternate region.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 updated: mitigation applied (kv-evict-mode=aggressive), canary deployed, scheduled maintenance window at 02:00 UTC. severity remains P2.

mike: final note — we should consider adding a background defragmenter to the paged-allocator that opportunistically coalesces free segments to reduce long-term drift. filing design RFC after this incident.

sasha: thanks all. will keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
